Questions: 1) TUYA is trading at 1.28x book value. If you subtract cash, the market values the business at $329M for $328M revenue and $63M earnings. That's essentially 1x revenue and 5.2x earnings for the operating business. Why so cheap? 2) Could the cash be trapped in China and inaccessible? 3) The $37M dividend ($0.06/share) is being paid from cash reserves, not earnings. Is this a capital return or a slow liquidation? 4) Why isn't an activist investor demanding a special dividend or buyback? 5) Is this a 'cash box' that could be privatized?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a special situations analyst. Focus on the extreme cash position and whether it represents real shareholder value or trapped capital.

tasks.prompt: GRAB $500M BUYBACK ANALYSIS: Announced Feb 2025. $500M = 3.4% of $14.7B market cap. At $3.60/share, that's 138.9M shares = 3.5% of 3.96B outstanding. Questions: 1) How much has Grab actually bought back so far? Any 10-Q or 8-K filings showing progress? 2) At current prices, $500M buys more shares than at higher prices — is this accretive? 3) $500M vs $6.47B cash = only 7.7% of cash. Is this too small? Should Grab do $2B? 4) How does the buyback affect EPS? If they retire 139M shares, what's the new EPS? 5) Is the buyback creating a price floor? 6) Compare to Uber's buyback history and impact on stock price.
tasks.system_prompt: You are a capital allocation analyst. Focus on buyback mechanics and impact on per-share metrics.

tasks.prompt: TUYA DIVIDEND DEEP DIVE: Current yield 5.48%. Dividend $0.121/share ($37M annual). Payout ratio 112% (exceeds earnings!). Cash payout ratio 90.2%. FCF only $21.2M (dividend is $37M, so dividend > FCF). But company has $951M cash so it can pay dividends for 25+ years from cash alone. Questions: 1) Is this dividend sustainable? It exceeds both earnings AND FCF. 2) Are they paying dividends from cash reserves rather than operations? Is this value-destructive? 3) Special dividend of $0.054 in Aug 2025 PLUS regular $0.0608 — are they aggressively returning cash? 4) For a CN_ADR, is the dividend a signal that cash is real and accessible? 5) At 5.48% yield, is TUYA better than a bond for income investors? 6) Will the dividend be cut if earnings don't grow?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a dividend analyst. Focus on sustainability, coverage ratios, and whether the dividend signals cash accessibility for a Chinese company.

tasks.prompt: GRAB vs GOTO (GOJEK-TOKOPEDIA): GoTo is Grab's biggest competitor in Indonesia (largest SE Asian market). Questions: 1) How does Grab's Indonesia market share compare to GoTo? 2) GoTo went public via SPAC too — how has it performed vs Grab? 3) Which company is winning in food delivery, ride-hailing, and payments in Indonesia? 4) Could GoTo and Grab merge? What would that mean for shareholders? 5) How does competition in Indonesia affect Grab's margins? 6) Is GoTo's fintech (GoPay, GoFinance) ahead of or behind GrabPay?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a Southeast Asian competitive analyst. Focus on market share dynamics in Indonesia and the broader competitive landscape.

tasks.prompt: TUYA KILL TEST: Apply kill criteria. Kill if: 1) Chronic dilution >10%/yr — check share count trends. 2) CEO selling at bottom — Jerry Wang owns 19.4%, is he selling? 3) Reverse split history — any? 4) Negative unit economics — 47.8% GM, 19.1% net margin, positive. 5) Fraud/SEC — any VIE risks, delisting threats? 6) Zombie company — generating $62.6M net income, paying dividends. 7) CN_ADR penalty: -10 points in our scoring system. Does the China risk alone warrant a KILL? For each: PASS or FAIL.

tasks.prompt: GRAB EARNINGS QUALITY: SimplyWallSt flagged 'High level of non-cash earnings' as a risk. Net income $380M but FCF is volatile ($329M annual, but quarterly swings from -$159M to +$69M). Questions: 1) What portion of net income is non-cash (SBC, deferred tax, mark-to-market on investments)? 2) The Q4'25 $172M net income spike — was this driven by investment gains or one-time items? 3) Reconcile: If NI is $380M and annual FCF is $329M, what's the $51M gap? Is it capex, SBC, or other? 4) Would you say GRAB's earnings are 'high quality' (backed by cash) or 'low quality' (accounting profits)? 5) What's the 'adjusted' or 'normalized' earnings power?
tasks.system_prompt: You are an earnings quality analyst. Focus on cash conversion, non-cash items, and the gap between reported and economic earnings.

tasks.prompt: PORTFOLIO HOLDINGS vs SIMPLYWALL ST FAIR VALUES: 1) GRAB: Current $3.60, Fair Value $5.97 (66% upside). 2) TUYA: Current $2.09, Fair Value $3.43 (64% upside). 3) BMBL: Current $3.04, Fair Value $9.00 (196% upside) [but our analysis says $5.95 EV]. Questions: 1) Are SimplyWallSt fair values reliable? What's their track record? 2) All three are ~40-60% undervalued per SimplyWallSt. Is this a coincidence or a structural bias in their model? 3) Which of our holdings has the most REALISTIC path to fair value? 4) If all three reached SimplyWallSt fair value, what would our portfolio be worth? 5) SimplyWallSt gives TUYA 6/6 valuation (perfect) and GRAB 4/6. Why the difference when both are ~40% undervalued?
tasks.system_prompt: You are a model validation analyst. Assess the reliability of DCF-based fair value estimates from SimplyWallSt. Compare to analyst consensus and our own analysis.

tasks.prompt: GRAB CONVICTION ASSESSMENT after analyzing all data. Rate your conviction (1-10) on each thesis: 1) Revenue will compound 15%+ for 5 years. 2) Profitability is sustainable and will expand. 3) The SE Asia superapp model creates a durable moat. 4) Fintech will become a major revenue driver. 5) The stock will be higher in 5 years. 6) The stock will be higher in 10 years. 7) The $500M buyback will support the price. 8) GRAB is better than holding cash for 10 years.
